tasks.question: Some people say social media makes us less sociable. What would you say against that?

cues.cue: social media / help / people stay in touch daily
models: I completely disagree that social media makes us less sociable, because it helps people stay in touch daily, which instead suggests it strengthens relationships rather than weakening them.

cues.cue: messaging apps / let / friends chat throughout the day
models: I strongly oppose the view that social media makes us less sociable, since messaging apps let friends chat throughout the day, and the evidence shows that many friendships are sustained almost entirely online.

cues.cue: video calls / allow / face-to-face contact across distances
models: I do not believe that social media makes us less sociable, because video calls allow face-to-face contact across distances, and in reality this keeps people closer than earlier generations ever were.

cues.cue: online groups / bring / like-minded people together
models: I disagree with the argument that social media makes us less sociable, as online groups bring like-minded people together, which means new friendships form that would never have existed otherwise.

cues.cue: platforms / encourage / organising real-life meetups
models: I am not convinced that social media makes us less sociable, given that platforms often encourage organising real-life meetups, and the data suggests heavy users socialise offline just as much as anyone else.

cues.cue: constant contact / keep / bonds alive
models: I strongly reject the idea that social media makes us less sociable, since constant contact with friends and family keeps bonds alive, and a better explanation is that other pressures, not social media, are behind any decline in socialising.

tasks.question: 'Studying abroad is always better than studying at home.' Do you disagree?

cues.cue: studying at home / offer / strong support networks too
models: I completely disagree that studying abroad is always better than studying at home, because studying at home offers strong support networks too, which instead suggests the choice depends on the individual.

cues.cue: local universities / provide / excellent programmes in many countries
models: It is inaccurate to claim that studying abroad is always better than studying at home, since local universities provide excellent programmes in many countries, and the reality is that quality varies far more by institution than by location.

cues.cue: living abroad / bring / high costs and homesickness
models: This viewpoint is difficult to accept because it fails to consider that living abroad brings high costs and homesickness, and many students thrive without ever leaving home.

cues.cue: family support / help / students cope with pressure
models: I do not share the opinion that studying abroad is always better than studying at home, because family support helps students cope with pressure, and in fact many perform better close to home.

cues.cue: studying abroad / place / financial burden on families
models: There are several reasons why I disagree with the claim that studying abroad is always better than studying at home, including the financial burden it places on families, and the fact that not every student adapts well to a new culture.

cues.cue: outcomes / depend / on the individual student
models: I am not convinced that studying abroad is always better than studying at home, given that outcomes depend heavily on the individual student, and the data suggests many top graduates never studied overseas.

tasks.question: Some claim that technology has made our lives less meaningful. What would you argue?

cues.cue: technology / connect / people across the world
models: I completely disagree that technology has made our lives less meaningful, because it connects people across the world, which instead suggests it has deepened rather than weakened human relationships.

cues.cue: medical technology / save / countless lives
models: I strongly oppose the view that technology has made our lives less meaningful, since medical technology saves countless lives, and the evidence shows this alone gives millions of families more meaningful time together.

cues.cue: creative tools / let / people express themselves in new ways
models: I do not believe that technology has made our lives less meaningful, because creative tools let people express themselves in new ways, and in reality this has opened up entirely new forms of meaning and connection.

cues.cue: technology / give / people access to knowledge instantly
models: It is inaccurate to claim that technology has made our lives less meaningful, since it gives people access to knowledge instantly, and the reality is that curiosity and learning have never been easier to pursue.

cues.cue: technology / support / people with disabilities
models: I strongly reject the idea that technology has made our lives less meaningful, since it supports people with disabilities in living fuller lives, and a better explanation is that meaning has simply shifted, not disappeared.

cues.cue: remote work / give / people more time with family
models: I disagree with the argument that technology has made our lives less meaningful, as remote work gives people more time with family, which means many now find daily life more fulfilling, not less.

tasks.question: Some say young people today are lazier than in the past. What would you say?

cues.cue: young people / juggle / study, work and family pressures
models: I completely disagree that young people today are lazier than before, because many juggle study, work and family pressures simultaneously, which instead suggests they are under more pressure than previous generations.

cues.cue: young people / build / businesses and skills online
models: I strongly oppose the view that young people today are lazier than before, since many build businesses and skills online in their spare time, and the evidence shows this takes real discipline and effort.

cues.cue: economic conditions / make / stable careers harder to achieve
models: I do not believe that young people today are lazier than before, because economic conditions make stable careers harder to achieve, and in reality many are working just as hard for far less security.

cues.cue: young people / volunteer / for causes at high rates
models: I strongly reject the idea that young people today are lazier than before, since they volunteer for causes at high rates, and a better explanation is that their priorities have simply changed, not their work ethic.

cues.cue: young workers / show / strong ambition in surveys
models: It is inaccurate to claim that young people today are lazier than before, since young workers show strong ambition in surveys, and the reality is that older generations often judge them by outdated standards.

cues.cue: young people / face / a far more competitive job market
models: There are several reasons why I disagree with the claim that young people today are lazier than before, including the fact that they face a far more competitive job market, and that they are adapting to challenges earlier generations never encountered.

tasks.question: 'Exams are the only real measure of ability.' Do you disagree?

cues.cue: coursework / show / a student's ability over time
models: I completely disagree that exams are the only real measure of ability, because coursework shows a student's ability over time, which instead suggests that ability cannot be reduced to a single test.

cues.cue: exams / cause / unfair pressure on some students
models: I strongly oppose the view that exams are the only real measure of ability, since exams cause unfair pressure on some students, and the evidence shows this often distorts what is actually being measured.

cues.cue: practical projects / reveal / skills exams cannot capture
models: I do not believe that exams are the only real measure of ability, because practical projects reveal skills exams cannot capture, and in reality many talented students underperform under exam conditions.

cues.cue: some highly capable students / struggle / with exam pressure
models: It is inaccurate to claim that exams are the only real measure of ability, since some highly capable students struggle with exam pressure, and the reality is that this says more about test anxiety than ability.

cues.cue: portfolios / demonstrate / creativity and problem-solving
models: I disagree with the argument that exams are the only real measure of ability, as portfolios demonstrate creativity and problem-solving, which means ability shows itself in far more than written tests.

cues.cue: many successful people / perform / poorly in exams
models: I am not convinced that exams are the only real measure of ability, given that many successful people performed poorly in exams, and the data suggests other forms of assessment can be just as revealing.
